This matter is taken up by hybrid mode.

08.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3.

The petitioners have filed this writ petition seeking to quash Annexures-5 and 6 and to issue direction to opposite party no.3 to deposit the money as per the revised 3-G award and also to direct opposite party no.4 to disburse the same in favour of the petitioners.
4. Mr. B.K. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that though the lands of the petitioners have been acquired, till date compensation amount has not been paid.
It is contended that initially interim order was granted, but subsequently this Court vacated the same and called upon the opposite parties to produce the record with regard to acquisition of land.

It is contended that whatever compensation amount has been determined and award has been passed,
the petitioners are willing to receive the same.
The same having not been disbursed, the petitioners have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

5. Ms. S. Pattnaik, learned Addl. Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties contended that compensation amount has already been determined by the authority and though the authority wants to disburse the same, the petitioners are not willing to receive the same, although three land losers have received the same.

6. Mr. U.C. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.3 contended that on the basis of the award passed by the authority under Section 3-G of the Act, notices have been issued to the Sushanta Kumar Mohanta And vs State Of Odisha And Others ..... ...

Therefore, steps have been taken by way of paper publication enabling the petitioners to approach the authority for receiving the compensation amount, as determined by the authority.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that the lands of the petitioners have been acquired and compensation amount has already been determined and though three of the land losers have already received the amount, the petitioners have not yet received the same in spite of notice issued by the authority.
Mr. B.K. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the petitioners are willing to receive the awarded amount.
8. In such view of the matter, the petitioners are directed to appear before opposite party no.4 at 10.30 A.M. on 20.03.2024.
If the petitioners appear on the date fixed, opposite party no.4 shall disburse the compensation amount in their favour.
In the event, the petitioners claim for higher compensation, it shall be open for them to pursue their remedy before the appropriate forum in accordance with law.
9. With the aforesaid liberty, the writ petition stands disposed of.

Ashok (DR. B.R.
